summary: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are one- or two-year master's degrees run by consortia of universities, usually in two or three European countries. The EU funds full scholarships for the best-ranked applicants from anywhere in the world, worth €1,400 a month for the length of the programme.
covers: A scholarship calculated at €1,400 per month for the full programme duration (12, 18 or 24 months), meant for travel, visa, installation and living costs.
Participation costs (tuition, insurance and other mandatory fees) are covered for scholarship holders.
A joint or multiple degree from the universities in the consortium, with study periods in at least two countries.
eligibility: Open to students of any nationality with a bachelor's degree — or in the final year of one, graduating before the master's starts.
Each programme sets its own academic, subject and language requirements.
Anyone who has already held an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship cannot receive a second one.
Consortia must keep their scholarship holders geographically balanced — no more than 10% from a single nationality — so strong applicants from under-represented countries are not disadvantaged.
how_to_apply: Browse the Erasmus Mundus catalogue on the EACEA website and shortlist programmes that fit your background.
Apply directly to each programme through its own website — there is no central application.
Most programmes take applications between October and January for the following September, and scholarship applications usually close with the programme's first deadline.
Prepare a motivation letter tailored to that programme, references, transcripts and language certificates; some programmes also interview.
watch_out: Every consortium has its own deadline and document list. Keep a spreadsheet — applicants often apply to three or four programmes.
The scholarship is competitive and ranked; programmes also admit self-funded students, so an offer of admission is not an offer of a scholarship.
You will move between countries, so budget time for more than one residence permit.
